name: Indian Poker
description: Indian Poker (also known as Blind Man's Bluff) is a unique poker variant where each player holds their card(s) against their forehead facing outward, so they can see all opponents' cards but not their own. Players bet based on what they see others holding, creating a game of deduction and reverse psychology.

content.text: Indian Poker (also known as Blind Man's Bluff) is a unique poker variant where each player holds their card(s) against their forehead facing outward, so they can see all opponents' cards but not their own. Players bet based on what they see others holding, creating a game of deduction and reverse psychology.

Indian Poker is a modern variant of Blind Man's Bluff adapted to card play. The name 'Indian Poker' comes from the visual similarity to Native American headdresses when cards are held to the forehead. The game has no actual connection to India or Native American culture - it's simply a descriptive name for the way cards are held.

Minimum Players: 2
Maximum Players: 8
Optimal Players: 4-6
Partnerships: No

Type: Standard 52-card deck
Number of Decks: 1
Jokers: No

Standard 52-card deck
Poker chips for betting

Cards per Player: 1 (or more in variants)
Dealing Pattern: Each player receives one card face down
Card placement: Players hold cards to their foreheads without looking
